plan: [ In a 3-bidder, private-values, second-price auction with rational opponents, bidding one’s true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Overbidding risks winning at a price above value; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. With value = 3, bid 3. If there’s a tie at 3, winning yields zero surplus (price ≈ 3), which is acceptable and avoids negative payoff risk. No prior history to exploit in round 1; stick to truth-telling to maximize expected profit. ]

[ This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and rational opponents. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value: it guarantees I win exactly when my value is the highest and pay the second-highest bid, maximizing expected profit. Overbidding risks paying more than my value if I win; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With one round and no exploitable history, no strategic deviation is beneficial. If tied at the top, winner is random; truth-telling remains optimal. ]

[ This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. For risk-neutral, rational bidders, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of opponents’ strategies. Underbidding risks losing when you should win; overbidding risks winning and paying more than your value if the second-highest bid exceeds your value. With value = 11, the profit-maximizing bid is 11. ]
